The existing lab provides the addresses needed for the DNS hierarchy without changing its topology or routes. The implementation-ready specification is:

| Zone | Authoritative server | Existing IP |
|---|---|---|
| `.` | pc1 | `10.14.1.11` |
| `com` | pc2 | `10.14.1.12` |
| `net` | pc3 | `10.14.1.13` |
| `example.com` | pc4 | `10.14.1.14` |
| `service.com` | pc5 | `10.14.2.11` |
| `lab.net` | pc6 | `10.14.2.12` |
| `tools.net` | pc7 | `10.14.2.13` |
| `shop.example.com` | pc8 | `10.14.3.11` |
| `api.service.com` | pc9 | `10.14.3.12` |
| `research.lab.net` | pc10 | `10.14.3.13` |
| `ci.tools.net` | pc11 | `10.14.4.11` |
| `ai.research.lab.net` | pc12 | `10.14.4.12` |
| `data.research.lab.net` | pc13 | `10.14.4.13` |

Configure BIND using the existing `kathara/base` images. Each zone will have SOA and NS records; the 12 parent-to-child delegations will have the necessary glue. The five requested delegated names will have apex A records pointing to their respective servers.

Configure pc14 (`10.14.4.14`) as a recursive resolver using pc1 as its root hint, and configure pc16–pc20 to query it. Add the four priority-10 MX records and their specified A records. Point `www.example.com` to pc4 and start its existing Apache service. The requested mail support is interpreted as DNS mail routing; running an SMTP service would require an additional service choice and configuration.

Persist the DNS configuration in per-device filesystem directories and startup files, preserving `lab.conf`, addresses, links and routing. Validation would check zone syntax, each delegation and glue record, recursive resolution from the five clients, MX and A answers, and HTTP access to `www.example.com`.

May I create the configuration from this specification? The [Kathara creation skill](/var/folders/84/zz92dr1178v8z_tvd_q2dfw40000gn/T/kathara-aut-gv_kt8yi/lab/.codex/skills/kathara-creation/SKILL.md) explicitly separates the stages: “Only start creating files after the user asks to create the scenario starting from the generated prompt.” No files have been changed.
